note: Locked requirements. Status is never stored here: scripts/verify.py works it out from real test runs. Do not edit without David (see docs/04-VERIFICATION.md).

checks.claim: Python 3.11+ runs from .venv and every installed dependency imports
cmd: import sys, httpx, rich, dotenv, numpy, sounddevice, comtypes, faster_whisper; assert sys.version_info >= (3, 11); print('LIVE deps: PASS')

checks.claim: Jarvis keeps the conversation in mind: system prompt, then recent history, then the new message; only the last N turns are sent; /reset forgets; a reply cut short is still remembered
If a brain fails before answering Jarvis tries the next one; an empty reply counts as a failure; a failure mid-reply never splices two models together; all failing gives a clear error
The provider layer streams text from the OpenAI-style SSE format and turns HTTP and connection errors into plain-English reasons
Settings come from .env with sensible defaults, skip brains without keys, keep the configured order, and give clear errors for bad values
The system prompt tells Jarvis the user's name and the current time
setup.bat recognises Gemini and Groq key shapes (including the newer AQ. Gemini keys), hides keys when showing them, edits .env without losing comments, rejects bad keys and can add a backup key
The real cloud brain answers a real question using the key in .env
Recording stops after a pause following speech, gives up if nobody speaks, ignores a single click, adapts to a noisy room, stops at the maximum length, and writes 16 kHz mono 16-bit WAV
Streaming text is cut into sentences as soon as each ends, tolerates tokens split mid-word, does not split on abbreviations or decimals, and strips markdown and links before speaking
Speech engines are chosen automatically (Groq ears if a key exists, Kokoro only if downloaded), explicit choices win, and bad choices give clear errors
Spoken audio is transcribed correctly by the real local Whisper model (Windows speaks a sentence into a WAV, Whisper must hear 'Japan')
The Windows voice speaks a sentence without error (the script cannot hear it; P2-H2 covers that)
Speech in to answer out works end to end within the time limit set in scripts/live_checks.py (heard 'capital of Japan', answered Tokyo)
With his own voice and real microphone, David asks 5 real questions through voice.bat and gets a spoken answer each time
checks.steps: Double-click voice.bat, press Enter, ask a question aloud, pause. Repeat 5 times with different questions.

checks.claim: The voice is clearly audible, British, and no sentence is cut off in the middle
checks.steps: During P2-H1 listen for volume, accent and clipped sentences.

checks.claim: The wake detector fires once when the score crosses the threshold, ignores a second spike inside the 2 second cooldown, and fires again after it
checks.must_assert: feed fake score frames; count of fires is exactly 1 for two spikes 1.0 s apart and exactly 2 for two spikes 2.5 s apart

checks.claim: The wake detector never fires below the threshold, including a single noisy spike just under it
checks.must_assert: scores of 0.49 with threshold 0.5 produce zero fires, including one isolated 0.49 spike amid zeros

checks.claim: While Jarvis is speaking the detector ignores scores, and when speech ends its buffer is cleared so Jarvis cannot wake on its own voice
checks.must_assert: a high score while paused gives zero fires; after resume the same high score from stale buffered audio gives zero fires; a fresh high score gives one

checks.claim: The wake chime is generated in code: 16 kHz, between 0.1 and 0.6 seconds, and not silent
checks.must_assert: length in samples within bounds and max absolute amplitude greater than 0.05

checks.claim: WAKE_THRESHOLD, JARVIS_WAKE and JARVIS_VOICE_SPEED have defaults and give clear errors for bad values such as 'high' or 1.7
checks.must_assert: defaults 0.5 / on / 1.1; ValueError messages name the setting and the bad value

checks.claim: One shared microphone stream feeds 1,280-sample frames, and the recorder makes the same stop decisions from stream frames as it does today
checks.must_assert: frames are exactly 1280 samples; the same synthetic speech+pause input yields the same stop index through the stream path and the existing path

checks.claim: If the wake model cannot load, voice.bat falls back to press-Enter mode with a one-line explanation instead of crashing
checks.must_assert: force the loader to raise; the run function returns normally, selects enter mode, and the console output contains a reason

checks.claim: Speech speed is adjustable: the Windows voice maps speed to SAPI Rate (-10 to +10, clamped) and the Kokoro voice passes the speed factor to synthesis
checks.must_assert: 1.0 maps to Rate 0, 1.5 maps to a positive Rate, out-of-range values are clamped; a fake Kokoro receives speed=1.25 in create()

checks.claim: Jarvis can list installed voices and switch between them
checks.must_assert: list_voices() returns the names the fake engine reports; switching changes which voice speaks the next sentence

checks.claim: In voice mode the system prompt tells Jarvis the real commands for changing voice and speed, so it never claims the feature does not exist
checks.must_assert: the voice-mode prompt contains /voice and /speed and the current voice name; text mode does not

checks.claim: The real wake model detects 'Hey Jarvis' spoken by Windows into a WAV, then the recorder and Whisper transcribe the question after it
From about 2 metres in a quiet room, saying 'Hey Jarvis' wakes it at least 8 times out of 10
checks.steps: Stand 2 m from the laptop. Say 'Hey Jarvis' 10 times, 5 seconds apart. Write down how many woke it.

checks.claim: With a TV or music playing for one hour, it wakes by itself fewer than about once
checks.steps: Leave voice.bat running for an hour with normal TV or music. Count unprompted chimes.

checks.claim: Jarvis never wakes on its own voice while speaking a long answer
checks.steps: Ask for a long explanation (30+ seconds). No chime may sound while it speaks.

checks.claim: Speed and voice can be changed by command and the difference is audible; asking 'how do I change your voice?' gets a correct answer
checks.steps: Type /speed 1.4, /voices, /voice <name>. Then ask aloud how to change the voice.

checks.claim: Only registered tools can run, and their arguments are validated before anything executes
checks.must_assert: an unknown tool name raises ToolError and runs nothing; wrong argument types and out-of-range values are rejected with a message naming the argument

checks.claim: Anything that deletes, sends or spends needs a spoken yes first; a tool with no declared risk level defaults to needing confirmation
checks.must_assert: a confirm-first tool called without a yes performs no side effect (checked on a fake); after a yes it runs once; an unlabeled tool behaves as confirm-first

checks.claim: Every tool call is logged with name, arguments and result to data/tool-log.jsonl, and secrets never appear in the log
checks.must_assert: after a call the log has one JSON line with the three fields; a key-shaped argument is replaced by a placeholder

checks.claim: Opening apps and folders is limited to an allowlist, never uses a shell, and refuses paths outside allowed folders
checks.must_assert: a non-allowlisted app name is refused; subprocess is called with an argument list; a path with .. or outside the allowed roots is refused

checks.claim: Time, weather and web search tools return correct structured data from fake responses, and search results are marked as untrusted data
checks.must_assert: time uses the Africa/Nairobi zone; weather parsing of a recorded Open-Meteo payload gives the expected numbers; search results are wrapped so the model is told they are data not instructions

checks.claim: Timers fire after the right delay, and reminders survive a restart
checks.must_assert: with a fake clock a 60 s timer fires at 60 s and not before; a reminder written by one connection is read by a new one

checks.claim: Streamed tool calls from the model are assembled, executed, fed back, and the loop stops after a maximum number of steps
checks.must_assert: split tool_call deltas reassemble into one call; the result is sent back and the final answer streams; a model that always asks for a tool stops at the step limit with a clear message

checks.claim: The 'Honesty' paragraph of the prompt lists exactly the tools that are registered, so Jarvis neither denies nor invents abilities
checks.must_assert: for every registered tool its name appears in the prompt, and abilities that are not registered are still described as not connected

checks.claim: The real brain, given the tools, answers 'what time is it' by calling the time tool and the answer contains the real current hour
By voice: 'Open Chrome and search for flights to Mombasa' works
checks.steps: Say it. Chrome opens on a search page for the query.

checks.claim: By voice, asking Jarvis to delete a file makes it ask for confirmation out loud and nothing is deleted before the yes
checks.steps: Create a junk file. Ask Jarvis to delete it. Say no first (file must remain), then repeat and say yes.

checks.claim: A remembered fact survives closing and reopening the database
checks.must_assert: write with one Memory object, open a new one on the same file, the fact is returned

checks.claim: Recall finds the relevant fact by keyword and does not return unrelated ones
checks.must_assert: after storing three different facts, recall('sister') returns only the sister fact

checks.claim: Forgetting removes a fact and it is never recalled again
checks.must_assert: after forget, recall returns nothing for that fact, including after reopening the file

checks.claim: Profile facts are loaded into the system prompt at startup
checks.must_assert: a stored profile fact appears in the prompt text

checks.claim: Memory refuses to store API keys, passwords and card numbers
checks.must_assert: strings shaped like AIza/AQ./gsk_ keys, 'my password is ...' and 16-digit card numbers are rejected and not written

checks.claim: A session summary is saved and can be retrieved in a later session
checks.must_assert: summary text stored at end of one session is returned by search in a new Memory object

checks.claim: Memory persists across two separate Python processes using a real database file
After quitting and restarting Jarvis it still knows David's name, a stated preference and yesterday's reminder
checks.steps: Tell Jarvis a fact. Quit. Start it again. Ask about the fact.

checks.claim: The screen tool captures, downsizes and encodes a screenshot for the vision model
checks.must_assert: with a fake capture, the output is a base64 data URL whose decoded image is no wider than the configured maximum

checks.claim: The camera opens only on an explicit request and is always released afterwards, even when capture fails
checks.must_assert: no camera is opened at import or startup; after a successful and after a failing capture release() was called

checks.claim: Images are sent to the provider in the correct base64 message format
checks.must_assert: the request body contains an image_url part whose url starts with data:image/

checks.claim: Images are never written to disk unless the user asked to save one
checks.must_assert: a temp directory is empty after a normal look; a file exists only after an explicit save request

checks.claim: The real vision model reads text from an image (a generated image containing ERROR 4417 must be read back as 4417)
Asked 'what is this error on my screen?' with a real error visible, Jarvis describes it correctly and suggests a fix
checks.steps: Open a real error message, ask aloud, judge the answer.

checks.claim: Only David's chat id is answered; everyone else is ignored silently
checks.must_assert: an update from another chat id produces no brain call and no reply

checks.claim: A text message reaches the brain and the reply is sent back
checks.must_assert: with a fake API, one text update leads to exactly one sendMessage carrying the brain's reply

checks.claim: A voice note is transcribed before it is asked
checks.must_assert: the audio is passed to the transcriber and its text, not the audio, reaches the brain

checks.claim: The bot token never appears in logs or error messages
checks.must_assert: force a network error; the captured log and exception text do not contain the token

checks.claim: The polling loop survives network errors with backoff instead of crashing or spinning
checks.must_assert: three consecutive failures lead to increasing waits and then a normal update is still processed

checks.claim: From his phone, David texts 'what's on my reminders?' and gets the right answer while the PC is on
checks.steps: Send the message from Telegram on the phone.

checks.claim: The visualizer's event bus holds the current state, delivers changes to subscribers and drops dead ones
The local visualizer server serves its page, streams states over SSE, finds a free port and survives clients disconnecting abruptly
The voice loop reports idle, listening, thinking, speaking and error states to the visualizer
The full HUD shows a transcript of what David said and what Jarvis answered
checks.must_assert: set_state or a new publish_transcript call produces an SSE message with role and text

checks.claim: Tool calls appear live in the HUD tool log
checks.must_assert: running a fake tool publishes an event with the tool name, arguments and outcome

checks.claim: The HUD shows CPU, memory and which brain is in use
checks.must_assert: a stats snapshot has numeric cpu and ram fields within 0 to 100 and the name of the active brain

checks.claim: Jarvis can be set to start with Windows and the setting can be removed cleanly
checks.must_assert: in a temp Startup folder a shortcut is created and then removed, and nothing outside the folder changes

checks.claim: During a real conversation the orb visibly changes with listening, thinking and speaking
checks.steps: Run voice.bat, hold a conversation, watch the browser window.

checks.claim: David has reviewed screenshots of the finished HUD at 1440x900 and 390x844 and approves the look
checks.steps: Open the screenshots the agent saved under docs/images and decide.

checks.claim: A scheduled job fires at its time and not before
checks.must_assert: with a fake clock a 07:00 job has not run at 06:59 and has run once by 07:01

checks.claim: Nothing is spoken during quiet hours
checks.must_assert: a job due at 02:00 is held until quiet hours end and not spoken at 02:00

checks.claim: The morning briefing is built from the weather and reminders tools, not made up
checks.must_assert: with fake tools returning known values, those values appear in the briefing text

checks.claim: Jarvis never talks over David: it waits until the microphone and speaker are idle
checks.must_assert: while the fake mouth reports speaking or the mic reports activity the announcement is held, and released after idle

checks.claim: Nudges (such as 'you have been coding for 3 hours') are off by default and rate-limited when on
checks.must_assert: default config schedules no nudges; when enabled, two triggers within the minimum gap produce one announcement

checks.claim: At 7 am Jarvis greets David with the day's weather and reminders without being asked
checks.steps: Leave Jarvis running overnight with the briefing enabled.
